title: Prove one rank-q internal map raises the paired-star external bound to q(g-1)
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->

## Change and mathematical scope

Proof, not a κ change. On the paired-star one-gap schedule of open PR #7025, one internal matrix `Z` of rank at most `q` cannot cancel the external remainder on its three helped leaves.

A successful word needs `P_s Z P_f = 0`: the degree-2 part of the internal product is that operator, supported on the stage, and the full-call bracket between the halves has no square. Under that equation each of the three core blocks has rank at most `q`, and their ranks sum to at most `3q`. Each helped leaf therefore still demands external rank at least `q`, and the heavier of the even and odd demand sums is at least `q(g-1)` for every gap placement.

At `g=31`, `q=26` this is external rank at least `780`, which is `2q = 52` above the dropped-leaf count `q(g-3) = 728`. The inequality system is sharp at stage 1: an explicit gap tuple meets every leaf demand at total `q(g-1)`, and lowering any positive gap breaks a leaf. That tuple is not a word.

The selected frontier stays `κ = 781451/250000000 = 0.003125804` (PR #6030). This does not construct a word of external rank 780, does not cover several rank-at-most-`q` maps in the same gap, and does not replace the consecutive-rank theorem of #7005.

## Task and overlap

- Base: `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840` (upstream `CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds` main, re-fetched before push; unchanged).
- Package: `research/paired-star-internal-three-blocks`.
- Task card: `joint-query-controller`, catalogue priority revision 8, `scope_status: changed`. The card premise is not this schedule; the assigned question is the three-leaf internal contribution of #7025.
- Neighbor: #7025 (`ec8ab41023fcf244e2bf790b13e829127d2e08e4`, `research/g31-q26-internal-gap`) gives external count `q(g-3)` after one gap leaves at least `g-3` leaves outside. This package starts from that count and bounds the three core blocks.
- Not redone: the one-gap count of #7025 and the consecutive-rank theorem of #7005. Not taken: every-stage rank, `g=13` remainders, interleaved or nested/crossing schedules.
- Source pins are files at the base commit only. No external head pin. Provenance: `certificates/selected-result.json`, `docs/research/agent-task-catalog.json`, `research/coupled31-chronology/PROOF.md`.
- `docs/research/current-priorities.md` is still labelled revision 8 and quotes an older κ. The selected record above is the one used.
- Fork `main` is `f9701fe9b`, not upstream main. This draft is based on the pin `cursor/upstream-17469fff-base-6479` at exactly `17469fff` so the diff is only the new package.

## Validation

Evidence class: proof over any characteristic-2 field, for one matrix of rank at most `q`. The `q=1` census is an exhaustive check of that 8-by-8 matrix domain (all rank-at-most-1 matrices, all scalar `(B12, B21)`, both half orders). It is not a census of words. The explicit family and the gap-tuple check are inequality witnesses, not words.

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/paired-star-internal-three-blocks
```

Python 3.12, no dependencies. Both registered commands (`python -B` and `python -O -B`) print:

`PASS_INTERNAL_THREE_BLOCKS proof g=31 q=26 d=52 external_rank=780 dropped_leaf_rank=728 rank_sum_cap=78 q1_attained=18720`

`scripts/check_research_commit.py --ref HEAD` reports `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` for the six package files. `--check-source-history` was not completed: this checkout is shallow. The declared pins are the parent commit `17469fff`, and there is no external head pin.

Failure control: mutating the stage-1 equality tuple by decrementing one positive gap makes a leaf inequality fail, and the checker rejects that mutation.

## Credit

The one-gap schedule, the three blocks, and the count `q(g-3)` are from open PR #7025. The consecutive-rank theorem is #7005. Earlier paired-star work includes PR #5747 (Ali Romman) and #5673 / #5631 / #5617 (Cinna Davis).

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

1. Two rank-at-most-`q` matrices in the same gap, each with `P_s Z P_f = 0`: can every helped core block sum to rank `2q`? First step: add two copies of the rank-`q` witness on complementary core coordinates. If they do, #7025's `q(g-3)` still applies and this lift does not.
2. Does a gap tuple of total `q(g-1)` plus one rank-`q` internal matrix meet `I_d` on every core-to-leaf block at `g=31`, `q=26`? First step: stage 1, place the witness, and solve the even external gaps for a complement. This is not the every-stage question.
